title: Morning Edition
notes: Morning Edition for Friday, Nov 6, 2026. It covers developments since Thursday’s Morning Edition, especially events that moved from scheduled to completed.

The lead is Budget 2026, now tabled. Top stories: the White House Russia–Ukraine gathering, U.S. midterm counting, Hong Kong’s facial-recognition CCTV rollout, China’s forex-reserve hike, and Los Angeles’s mayoral upset.
Hong Kong has four stories; the U.S., Canada, China and World have three each. Culture appears in Canada and Hong Kong; there is no U.S. culture story this morning.
Some AP and Politico pages returned bot challenges (HTTP 403) in this run; we cite pages that did load and note access limits under Sources & checks.
provenance: Budget figures follow Department of Finance key-measures materials and CBC’s reading of the document; the full PDF was confirmed available (HTTP 200) but not fully text-extracted here.
House and Senate seat totals continue to move. CBS and NBC estimates are given with their sources; Donna Daily does not call races.
Xinhua items on the PBOC and CIIE are labelled State media. Joshua Wong court facts are separated from governments’ and NGOs’ statements about the sentence.

stories.headline: Carney government tables Budget 2026 as “Masters of Our Destiny”
stories.deck: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne tabled Budget 2026 in the Commons on Thursday, pitching nearly $142 billion in new multiyear spending and tax measures aimed at investment, affordability and reducing reliance on the United States.
stories.summary: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne tabled Budget 2026 in the Commons on Thursday, pitching nearly $142 billion in new multiyear spending and tax measures aimed at investment, affordability and reducing reliance on the United States. The official document is titled “Masters of Our Destiny.” Department of Finance key-measures materials highlight a Productivity Mega Deduction that would let businesses immediately deduct most new investments, a $25 billion Canada Strong Fund with retail Canada Strong Notes, more than $50 billion toward a national electricity strategy, and over $22 billion over five years in affordability measures including a one-time 50% top-up to the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit for 2026–27. CBC’s live coverage said the budget is the second under Prime Minister Mark Carney and draws criticism from opposition parties even as Liberals frame it as building the economy at home. Champagne’s tabled remarks ask for an order of the day to consider the ways-and-means motions.
stories.why: The budget is Ottawa’s main annual statement of spending and economic strategy, and it lands two days after a U.S. midterm that reshapes Canada’s closest trading partner.
stories.label: Official statement + reported
stories.note: Figures and measure names follow the Department of Finance key-measures backgrounder and Champagne’s tabled remarks; opposition reaction is as reported by CBC.

stories.headline: Melania Trump hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials; Trump says he met Putin’s envoy
stories.deck: The first lady gathered Russian and Ukrainian representatives at the White House on Thursday to mark a six-day Oleshky ceasefire and urged a “more enduring” peace. President Trump later said he met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev privately and predicted a larger deal, while saying he did not meet the Ukrainian delegation.
stories.summary: The first lady gathered Russian and Ukrainian representatives at the White House on Thursday to mark a six-day Oleshky ceasefire and urged a “more enduring” peace. President Trump later said he met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev privately and predicted a larger deal, while saying he did not meet the Ukrainian delegation. A White House statement said Melania Trump’s role as “Exclusive Intermediary” was written into agreements signed Oct. 23 and that nearly 800 people were evacuated during the pause, which both sides credit her with helping broker. BBC and NBC reported the guests included Dmitriev, Russia’s human-rights commissioner Yana Lantratova, Ukrainian MP Davyd Arakhamia and Ukraine’s human-rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets. Trump told reporters a coming agreement “might involve all of Europe.” NBC, citing Reuters, said U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi are scheduled for Nov. 10–11; Trump envoy Jared Kushner separately described “productive” Brussels talks on security guarantees.
stories.why: A rare White House meeting of wartime Russian and Ukrainian officials, plus Trump’s private session with a Putin envoy, will shape expectations for next week’s Abu Dhabi talks.
stories.label: Official statement + reported + claim
stories.note: Trump’s prediction of a Europe-wide agreement is his claim; no deal text has been published. White House wording on Melania Trump’s intermediary role is the administration’s account.

stories.headline: Democrats on pace for about 256 House seats as Mississippi and Alaska Senate races stay open
stories.deck: Three days after the midterms, CBS News estimates House Democrats are on track for around 256 seats after flipping more than 40 districts. Alaska and Mississippi remain the unresolved Senate contests, with Scott Colom leading Cindy Hyde-Smith by fewer than 2,000 votes as provisional and mail ballots are processed.
stories.summary: Three days after the midterms, CBS News estimates House Democrats are on track for around 256 seats after flipping more than 40 districts. Alaska and Mississippi remain the unresolved Senate contests, with Scott Colom leading Cindy Hyde-Smith by fewer than 2,000 votes as provisional and mail ballots are processed. CBS’s Thursday–Friday live updates said Democrats have flipped 43 House districts so far (two the other way), won at least 54 Senate seats, and that Mississippi still has roughly 3,600 outstanding mail ballots plus an unknown number of affidavit ballots, with county certification due by Nov. 13. NBC’s Decision Desk separately estimated Democrats will control at least 259 House seats and reported Mary Peltola leading Dan Sullivan by about 600 votes in Alaska. Race-by-race detail remains in our Midterms 2026 special.
stories.why: The remaining seats set the exact size of Democratic majorities and how much room leaders will have when the new Congress meets in January.
stories.label: Reported
stories.note: Donna Daily does not call races. Seat figures are as published by the linked outlets and will keep moving as ballots are counted.

stories.headline: Hong Kong police to switch on facial recognition across SmartView CCTV this month
stories.deck: Officers say AI facial recognition will roll out on the force’s roughly 10,000 SmartView cameras and linked feeds to help criminal searches and find high-risk missing people, with facial data kept for up to 180 days.
stories.summary: Officers say AI facial recognition will roll out on the force’s roughly 10,000 SmartView cameras and linked feeds to help criminal searches and find high-risk missing people, with facial data kept for up to 180 days. RTHK reported Superintendent Raymond Cheng saying the feature can be activated on police cameras and integrated third-party feeds but will be triggered only for active criminal searches or high-risk missing-person cases. CCTV footage itself will be kept for a maximum of 31 days. Police said at least four shopping malls have agreed to connect feeds; RTHK named Tuen Mun Town Plaza, Olympian City, Kwai Chung Shopping Centre and Sierra Life in Fanling. The force aims for about 60,000 public cameras by 2028.
stories.why: A citywide facial-recognition layer on public and some private cameras raises immediate questions about privacy, notice and how broadly “criminal search” will be defined.
stories.label: Official statement + reported
stories.note: Operational claims (pilot arrests, case counts) are as stated by police to RTHK and are not independently audited here.

stories.headline: PBOC raises foreign-currency reserve ratio to 6% as the yuan’s rally cools
stories.deck: China’s central bank will lift the forex deposit reserve requirement from 4% to 6% on Nov. 15 — its first increase in nearly five years — after a strong yuan run. The yuan’s central parity weakened to 6.7168 per dollar on Friday.
stories.summary: China’s central bank will lift the forex deposit reserve requirement from 4% to 6% on Nov. 15 — its first increase in nearly five years — after a strong yuan run. The yuan’s central parity weakened to 6.7168 per dollar on Friday. Xinhua reported the People’s Bank of China announced the 2-point increase on Nov. 3 as a macro-prudential tool to tighten dollar liquidity and ease upward pressure on the renminbi after a 4.2% gain against the dollar in the first nine months and a rapid October advance. A follow-up Xinhua note on Friday said the central parity slipped 12 pips to 6.7168.
stories.why: The reserve-ratio hike is a clear signal that Beijing wants to slow a one-way yuan rise without setting a hard exchange-rate target.
stories.label: State media + official statement
stories.note: PBOC policy details and parity figures are from Xinhua (state media). Market-impact commentary in secondary outlets is not treated as official guidance.

stories.deck: Kutryk and NASA astronaut Anil Menon completed a 6-hour, 59-minute extravehicular activity on Thursday, installing the eighth and final rollout solar array in an upgrade campaign that began in 2021.
stories.summary: Kutryk and NASA astronaut Anil Menon completed a 6-hour, 59-minute extravehicular activity on Thursday, installing the eighth and final rollout solar array in an upgrade campaign that began in 2021. The Canadian Space Agency had previewed the Nov. 5 spacewalk as a follow-up to the pair’s Oct. 29 outing. stories.summary: Alongside the growth agenda, the new budget proposes roughly $5 billion over five years for culture and heritage — including permanent free national-museum admission for people under 25, rink and recreation funding, and more money for CBC/Radio-Canada and local journalism. stories.headline: UK, US and EU condemn Joshua Wong’s 10-year sentence as Hong Kong officials hail the ruling
stories.deck: A day after Wong was jailed for conspiring to collude with foreign forces, Western governments and rights groups called the term cruel and political, while Chief Executive John Lee and security officials defended it as lawful punishment.
stories.summary: A day after Wong was jailed for conspiring to collude with foreign forces, Western governments and rights groups called the term cruel and political, while Chief Executive John Lee and security officials defended it as lawful punishment. BBC reported the High Court sentenced Wong to 10 years on Thursday, with just over two months concurrent with his existing subversion sentence; he had been due for release in January 2027. Hong Kong Free Press rounded up Friday reactions: Lee called Wong a “primary culprit” undermining stability; the UK Foreign Office and US Consulate condemned the prosecution; the EU urged respect for ICCPR and Joint Declaration commitments; Amnesty and Human Rights Watch called the sentence unjust.
stories.why: Wong is the most internationally known Hong Kong activist still imprisoned under the national security law, so the sentence and the diplomatic backlash will keep pressure on the city’s political reputation.
stories.label: Reported + official statement
stories.note: Conviction and sentence are court outcomes as reported; foreign governments’ and NGOs’ characterizations are their statements, not findings by Donna Daily.
